title: Quant Field Check-in (weekly research notes)
body:
Purpose:
Quick weekly capture for the applied-ml squad — focus this week on KV-prefetch microbenchmarks, 4-bit quantization stability on the QBench suite, and two model onboarding failures we hit in staging. Intended as a working log (notes + lightweight action items).

Meeting context:
- Weekly sync: Tue 06/03 10:30am (standup-format, 25m). Attendees: Aisha, Jonah, Marta, Wei, SRE: L. Gomez (brief).
- Main asks from infra: better failure diagnostics for oom vs kernel-fault during quantized loads.

Highlights (top-line):
- KV-prefetch proto reduced cold-start tokens by ~18% on GPT-like microbench (seq len 256, batch 4) in host-mode. Throughput improved but tail latency increased ~12ms p95 under bursty arrival — see "Experiments" for hypoth.
- QBench regression: 4-bit GPT-2-medium variant shows a BLEU-like metric dip of 2.3 points on the summarization eval after merging PR #98 (quant kernel reorder). Initial root cause points to softmax rounding noise in final layer when using per-channel scales.
- Model onboarding: two failures in staging for customer-demo models (onboarding ID: onboard-2025-05-29-a, onboard-2025-05-30-b). Both were configuration mismatches (wrong tokenizer config + missing KV cache init flag) — added preflight checks to onboarding job.

Experiments run this week (short notes):
1) KV-prefetch microbench (proto-0.3):
   - Setup: 1xA10, request pattern: bursty (Poisson with spikes), models: 2xGPT2-medium-like compiled with runtime v0.9.
   - Runs: 12 runs / 3 seeds each.
   - Results: median tokens/sec +11%, 95th latency +8-14ms depending on spike intensity. Cold-start token reduction ~18% (first 64 tokens). CPU offload usage increased 6%.
   - Hypothesis: prefetch increases early KV hits but contends with runtime I/O/lock during extreme concurrency; we need a non-blocking prefetch queue or reduce synchronous prefetch scope.
   - Next: try bounded async prefetch (proto-0.4) with backpressure = 2, and measure p95. Ticket: JIRA-ML-8820.

2) 4-bit quant stability (QBench v0.12):
   - Setup: quantization pipeline with per-channel symmetric int4, calibration on 2k tokens of domain data, eval on summarization/qa subsets.
   - Findings: observed downstream metric drift when quant kernel reorder flag enabled (PR #98). Running with reorder disabled restores metrics to baseline.
   - Debug notes: differences show up in logits at final layer ~1e-2 relative L2 in a subset of prompts. Suspect accumulation order + FP32->int4 rounding issues.
   - Mitigation possibilities: tweak reorder to use compensated summation, increase calibration samples, or move to mixed 8/4 scheme for sensitive layers.
   - Action: run layerwise sensitivity scan (ticket JIRA-ML-8809).

3) Onboarding failures postmortem:
   - Case A (onboard-2025-05-29-a): tokenizer.json had legacy 'gpt_tokenizer' field. Onboarding code assumed "tokenizer_type" key — resulted in fallback to byte-level tokenizer and mismatch with model vocab size. Fix: add tokenizer compatibility shim + clearer error message in onboarding logs. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/210.
   - Case B (onboard-2025-05-30-b): KV cache init disabled in YAML pipeline (env var not set). Caused repeated recompile loops and OOMs. Fix: onboarding preflight now fails fast if KV init not explicit.

Operational / infra notes:
- SRE asked for the following telemetry hooks to differentiate OOM vs kernel fault: 1) cropped stack trace with kernel module ID, 2) agent-level memory watermark before crash, 3) flag whether GPU page-faults observed. Adding to infra backlog (JIRA-OPS-431).
- Observability: added a prom counter kv_prefetch.backpressure_count (proto) so we can correlate p95 spikes with prefetch backpressure events.

Open questions / decision points:
- Should prefetch be default-on for hosted API? Current numbers show win for median cold-start but p95 hurt under spikes. Proposal: default-off; enable with route-level opt-in + recommended backpressure config. Preference from product: conservative rollout.
- Quant reorder trade: fix in kernel (longer) vs. switch to mixed precision for sensitive layers (faster). Need input from runtime team on kernel timeline.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Jonah: implement bounded async prefetch prototype (proto-0.4) and run p95 sweep (ETA: 2025-06-10).
- Marta: run layerwise sensitivity scan for reorder PR on QBench (JIRA-ML-8809) and produce per-layer delta CSV (ETA: 2025-06-09).
- Wei: add KV-prefetch prom counter + add quickstart dashboard panel for prefetch signals (ETA: 2025-06-08).
- Aisha: add onboarding preflight checks and tokenizer shim to model-onboard (PR drafted, review request sent) (ETA: 2025-06-06).
- SRE (L. Gomez): add memory/trace hooks to agent images for better crash classification (ops ticket JIRA-OPS-431) (ETA: 2025-06-17).

Quick sync notes from standup (bullet capture):
- Jonah: "proto-0.3 looks promising; need to fix lock contention and measure again".
- Marta: "reorder is the suspect; I can isolate a small prompt set that reproduces the delta every time".
- Wei: "dashboard up next; will add graphs for prefetch vs p95, and heatmap for kv cache hit ratio by prefix length".
- L. Gomez (SRE): "we can add a lightweight agent build with extra logging behind a feature flag — will coordinate infra schedule".

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a quick A/B on hosted API with safe fallback: route-level prefetch enabled + model variant fallback to non-prefetch variant if p95 above threshold for 5m. Could reduce customer impact while collecting data.
- For quant reorder kernel: add deterministic test in CI that compares final-layer logits across reorder toggles for a fixed seed + inputs; fail if L2 diff > 1e-3. Might catch regressions early.

Relevant snippets/logs (copied):
- from onboarding log (case B): "[ERROR] KV cache not initialised: onboarding aborting to avoid repeated OOMs (hint: set KVCACHE_INIT=true)"
- from proto run (p95 spike): "p95 172ms (with prefetch), p95 160ms (no prefetch) — backpressure_count=34 during 10s spike"

References / links: 
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-prefetch/pull/42
- Onboarding PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/210
- Jira: JIRA-ML-8809, JIRA-ML-8820, JIRA-OPS-431
- Slack threads: #applied-ml (thread ts: 1717400000.000200)

Closing note:
This doc is a working capture — will convert to a short public-ready summary if product wants a customer-facing blurb about prefetch improvements. For now keep experimental numbers internal.

-- Aisha
